findings.summary: The middleware-vs-dependency-vs-route-handler comparison is placed under 'Simplest Form' after the code, and 'Sees' row is vague, so it is unrelated to its section.
findings.evidence: 2. Simplest Form ... | Middleware | Dependency | Route handler / Scope | global | per-route | one route
findings.fix: Move the comparison table into its own section or into section 1 so it follows the idea it compares, and rename the 'Sees' row values to be specific (e.g. 'raw request, response' vs 'parsed params').

findings.summary: The ordering diagram labels and the bullet 'first middleware added is the innermost layer' are given as separate fragments, so the layered stack reads as a loose list.
findings.evidence: Request / Last added / outermost / First added / innermost / Endpoint
findings.fix: Render as one vertical stack diagram with arrows: Request → Last added (outermost) → ... → First added (innermost) → Endpoint.

findings.summary: A bullet holds two ideas: the body-buffering behaviour and the older-Starlette breakage.
findings.evidence: Reading await request.body() in BaseHTTPMiddleware buffers it in memory; older Starlette broke the endpoint
findings.fix: Split into two bullets: one for in-memory buffering, one for the older-version breakage.

findings.summary: Code for the pure ASGI class is shown before the idea of wrapping send is explained; the one-line idea appears only after the code.
findings.evidence: python class AddHeader: ... followed by 'wrap send to edit the response'; the explanation of http.response.start comes in section 2
findings.fix: State the idea (intercept http.response.start via a wrapped send) in a bullet before the code block.

findings.summary: Register bullet packs the registration call and the kwargs-to-__init__ rule into one line.
findings.evidence: Register: add_middleware(Cls, option=value); kwargs go to __init__(self, app, option)

findings.summary: The ordering example 'Register A then B: request path B → A → app' is stated in prose and repeated three ways; the table lists Auth as 'Registered 1st' with order 5 but the explanation of why is missing a visual of the stack.
findings.evidence: Last add_middleware call = outermost layer ... Request order is the reverse of registration; response order is registration order
findings.fix: Replace the repeated bullets with one diagram showing registration order on one side and request order on the other, with the A/B example.

findings.summary: The 500 Gap diagram is a list of unconnected labels and the explanation is in prose beneath it.
findings.evidence: ServerError / outside all / Your middleware / user stack / ExceptionMiddleware / HTTPException / Endpoint / raises / Missing headers on 500
findings.fix: Draw as a nested-box diagram (ServerErrorMiddleware > user middleware > ExceptionMiddleware > endpoint) and shorten the callout to one line.

findings.summary: The 'do not compress small or already-compressed data' advice is under the TrustedHost section at the end of the page, away from GZip where it belongs.
findings.evidence: Do not compress small or already-compressed data (images, zips): wastes CPU
findings.fix: Move it into section 1 GZipMiddleware, next to minimum_size.

findings.summary: GZip section shows code before stating the idea, and a bullet holds two ideas.
findings.evidence: 1. GZipMiddleware / python app.add_middleware(GZipMiddleware, ...) ; 'Adds Content-Encoding: gzip and Vary: Accept-Encoding'
findings.fix: Add a one-line purpose bullet before the code and split the header bullet into one bullet per header.

findings.summary: Code is shown before the handler concept is stated, and the first bullets pack several ideas.
findings.evidence: detail can be any JSON-serializable value, not only a string / headers= adds custom response headers / Handler is chosen by the exception class and its parents, then a code block
findings.fix: Lead with a one-line idea for each construct (custom exception handler; raising HTTPException) before its code, and split the combined code block into two.

findings.summary: The Starlette-vs-FastAPI HTTPException terminology is used loosely, so a skimmer may not know which class to import or handle.
findings.evidence: StarletteHTTPException | your raises, unknown-route 404s ... FastAPI HTTPException | only errors you raise
findings.fix: Add the import names (from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException) and state that FastAPI's HTTPException subclasses it.

findings.summary: Code for the error helper appears before the idea, and the request-id flow diagram is a loose list of labels.
findings.evidence: def error(status, code, message, details=()) ... ; Set ID / contextvar / Echo / X-Request-ID / Log / every line / Error body / request_id
findings.fix: State the one-envelope idea first, and render the request-ID flow as a left-to-right chain with arrows.

findings.summary: The ordering diagram repeats page 3 as unconnected labels and the 'Add in reverse' bullet is the only place stating the rule.
findings.evidence: Add in reverse: Auth first, TrustedHost last / TrustedHost / outermost / CORS / GZip / Request-ID / and logging / Auth / App / innermost
findings.fix: Render as a vertical stack with arrows and mark which end is registered first.

findings.summary: The 500 note is a prose paragraph with two ideas (ID reset, and the fix) that conflicts slightly with page 3's description of where the 500 response is built.
findings.evidence: The 500 handler runs outside user middleware: the ID is usually reset and no header is added. Catch errors inside the Request-ID middleware to keep the ID on 500s.
findings.fix: Split into two bullets: the problem and the fix, and use the same term for the outer layer (ServerErrorMiddleware) as on page 3.
